rv.q: Thomas’ performance is really something to experience in this piece and a work of real surety and depth coming at a time when most theaters are making a still-tentative recovery.
Throughout, “Songs for Nobodies” provides a vivid reminder of what we missed during the year+ of COVID-cancellations and a thrilling celebration of theater’s return.
Thomas clearly has found her own star vehicle in “Songs for Nobodies.”

Bethany Thomas magically transforms her towering presence into the size and vaulted styles of each singer, performing with such intensity, emotion and authority that we are joyfully reassured the power of live theatre, struggling mightily to return, will live on.
Breathtaking, startling, stunning, astonishing — this writer can't think of enough synonyms to say Thomas amazes.
Songs for Nobodies has a dreamlike quality as Thomas seamlessly negotiates the shifts between storyteller and singer.
The versatile Thomas confronts this challenging mimicry with spot-on accuracy, from Piaf's chesty croon to Holiday's kittenish whine...

Thomas constantly dazzles with her acting and vocal versatility throughout “Songs for Nobodies,” and she provides a convincing reason for theatergoers to venture back to Skokie following the pandemic shutdown.
Finally she has the stage all to herself and she seizes the moment to score a stunning personal triumph.
This is an extraordinary evening of music and storytelling and Ms Thomas truly shines in every way.

cn.t: Thomas delivers a bravura, powerhouse performance in this engaging one-woman show, nimbly channeling five iconic singers through stories of the "nobodies" who met them, though the vehicle demands more versatility than depth.
